cron_timing_note: Cron runs in UTC. One-shot crons scheduled 5-8 minutes ahead on specific minutes, read once via the cron-jobs output operation, then deleted immediately — none left armed (verified empty via a cron-jobs list call after smoke-test-live). One migrate-apply create-cron call in this deploy failed client-side with a transient DNS error (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND developers.hostinger.com) before reaching Hostinger at all; a cron-jobs list call confirmed no job had actually been created, so the retry was safe and did not double-schedule anything — worth that same list-to-confirm check any time a cron-create call itself errors, rather than assuming it's safe (or unsafe) to retry blind. 2026-10-03 addendum: a one-time cron whose minute has already passed never fires and its output stays empty forever (it happened twice, because the gap between reading the clock and creating the cron was many minutes). Schedule >=10-12 minutes ahead, create the cron immediately after reading the clock, and confirm by an ls/file-API probe instead of assuming. A `* * * * *` job running a harmless command is a fast way to read server state; delete it after. `%` in a cron command is eaten by crontab. TUS upload credentials stop working (403) well before their 6 h expiry.

Now: stage records a hash manifest; switch runs a three-way merge (snapshot / live / staged) until convergence BEFORE the rename, the two renames recover from a stray application directory, and additive post-rename sweeps (immediately, after 10 s, and in smoke-test-live) prove nothing is left only in the retired tree. Collisions are never overwritten (switch refuses before renaming; `keep-both` preserves the other copy under _upload-conflicts/). reconcile <retired> recovers files an older release stranded. See deploy/README.md 'Uploads during a deploy'.

membership_public_cache_2026_10_05.summary: Owner task 2026-10-05: fix Membership Season / public membership page cache invalidation completely. Root cause measured on production BEFORE any change: lib/api/membership.ts fetched the open seasons with next.revalidate 60 s and the types/fees with 300 s, no tags, and nothing told the site about admin changes; the page stayed stale 62.9 s after an admin opened a season and 61.7 s after closing it, and after a quiet period the FIRST request after a change was stale in both languages (stale-while-revalidate) while Laravel already answered correctly. Cloudflare served the HTML and the API as DYNAMIC (no Age; page Cache-Control private, no-store; API no-cache, private) — the only stale layer was Next's server-side data cache.
membership_public_cache_2026_10_05.design: (1) admin changes: observers -> tags -> ONE signed v2 call (nonce, replay guard, allow-list, 1-8 tags; legacy v1 still accepted) sent before the admin's response on the membership screens; the site expires the tags with revalidateTag(tag, {expire: 0}). (2) the clock: both lookups carry meta.valid_until and the site never uses a cached copy past it (it asks Laravel again, uncached) — no cron, no polling. (3) a 15 s safety-net window. (4) Laravel is the only authority at submit: a season is required and must be open at that moment; the form says so when Laravel refuses (data-testid=season-closed), where before it showed nothing at all.

found_not_fixed.recruitment_pdf_with_a_large_photo: On production, the recruitment application PDF of application 70 answers 500 in both languages (application 71's PDF is fine, 282 KB): mPDF refuses the document — 'The HTML code size is larger than pcre.backtrack_limit 1000000' (Mpdf.php:27018) — because the applicant photo is embedded in the HTML as a base64 data URI and a phone-camera photo alone passes 1 MB. The check runs on the HTML string before any font is touched, so it is independent of this release and was there before it; found while verifying (headers and bytes only, nothing saved or read) that the shared PDF engine still serves real recruitment applications. NOT fixed: out of this task's scope (receipt HTML is tens of KB). The fix is small and standard (resize the embedded photo for the document, or raise pcre.backtrack_limit / write the HTML in chunks) — the owner's call. Two ERROR lines from this check sit in storage/logs/laravel.log at 2026-10-09 06:58:26.
